sources.confirmed: Docker documents private PID namespaces by default and explicit joining of another container's PID namespace using --pid=container:<name|id>. This gives an implementation precedent for preserving PID 1 unless sharing is enabled.

sources.title: Docker/Moby private-or-container PID namespace modes
sources.sections_read: PID namespace branch in OCI configuration generation
sources.confirmed: Container PID mode resolves the target container and sets the OCI PID namespace path to /proc/<target PID>/ns/pid; private mode supplies a PID namespace without a path, while host mode removes it. When user namespaces are enabled, the joining container also joins the target user namespace.
sources.limits: Docker exposes this at container scope, so an orchestrator must derive every container's setting from the single pod option; the referenced implementation also joins the target user namespace when user namespaces are enabled. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C06.json.

sources.title: rkt pod-scoped namespace owner and application launch architecture
sources.sections_read: Stage1 systemd/nspawn flavor and application launch
sources.confirmed: rkt starts a pod-scoped systemd as PID 1 and has it launch the pod applications, retaining application-specific resource isolation. This demonstrates a pod namespace owner distinct from application entrypoints, but its general init behavior is beyond the requested scope.
sources.limits: The demonstrated implementation uses systemd/nspawn and includes general init behavior; only its namespace ownership and launch arrangement transfer to this task, and it does not itself preserve PID 1 assumptions for applications in shared mode. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C06.json.

sources.title: Linux PID namespace init and procfs semantics
sources.version_or_date: man-pages-4.15; header date verified separately as 2017-11-26
sources.sections_read: Namespace init, signal semantics, and /proc mounting
sources.confirmed: The namespace's first process receives PID 1; its exit kills the namespace's other processes, and PID 1 has special signal handling. A procfs instance presents the processes visible from the namespace of its mounter, so mount selection must agree with the intended process view.
sources.limits: One shared namespace has only one PID 1, so multiple applications that require their own PID 1 cannot retain that assumption in shared mode; leaving sharing disabled is the compatible path. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C06.json.

sources.title: util-linux nsenter for selective namespace-aware operations
sources.confirmed: nsenter starts a program in selected namespaces of a target process and forks by default when entering its PID namespace so the executed program receives the intended namespace. It provides a selective operational entry mechanism, not permanent sharing for all applications.
sources.limits: It requires an authorized caller able to enter the target namespace and does not provide mutual process visibility to all applications; its default fork when entering a PID namespace is essential to placing the helper correctly. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C06.json.

sources.title: Linux setns PID namespace joining semantics
sources.sections_read: .TH date; PID namespace reassociation and user-namespace restrictions
sources.confirmed: The 2017-09-15 manual explains that joining a PID namespace changes the namespace of future children rather than that of the caller, with descendant-namespace restrictions. This constrains the order of namespace setup and application process creation.
sources.limits: The documented descendant-namespace restrictions require a suitably placed runtime process; changing a running application's PID namespace is not a substitute for setting up its namespace at launch. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C06.json.

sources.title: OCI Runtime Specification v1.0.0 namespace path contract
sources.confirmed: OCI v1.0.0 distinguishes joining an existing namespace via an absolute path, creating a new namespace when the type is listed without a path, and inheriting the runtime namespace when a type is omitted. Its PID-path example provides a portable runtime representation for a pod-wide sharing policy.
sources.limits: A listed PID namespace without a path creates a namespace, while omitting the PID namespace inherits the runtime's namespace; those cases must not be confused, and the specification does not define pod ownership or lifecycle. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C06.json.
